title: Hermes
subtitle: hermes-agent (OSS) + Langfuse + HITL
description: Nous Research's hermes-agent is the open-source harness (MIT-licensed) — what's here is what I built around it: a nightly Langfuse eval loop and a weekly cron that clusters the agent's own low-quality turns and proposes edits to its own system prompt, on a 3-node homelab with a hand-patched local inference layer. Proposals still wait on me in Telegram before anything touches the live prompt.

title: Inference Engine
subtitle: llama.cpp + ROCm + Local Agentic Workflows
description: Three models resident on one box, serving every agent I run at $0 marginal cost per call — which changes which experiments are worth running at all. It's a hand-patched llama.cpp build on an AMD APU the project doesn't officially support: the dense 27B model should be capped at 7.4 tokens/sec by memory bandwidth alone. It isn't. Reachable from my phone over Telegram, every call traced, and nothing sensitive leaves the LAN.

title: Pi-Cloud
subtitle: Private Infrastructure + Service Operations
description: A Raspberry Pi 5 running 23 containers across 12 Compose projects — photos, passwords, document search, DNS filtering, private search, remote access, monitoring — with zero public ports and two recovery paths kept on deliberately different filesystems. Three of those services aren't just mine: SearXNG, ChromaDB, and Crawl4AI are the search, memory, and page-extraction backends an always-on agent calls unattended, which sets a higher bar than personal infra would. Verified 2026-07-25: every container carries a restart policy, so a reboot brings the whole stack back with no manual intervention.

title: Job-Fit Scorer
subtitle: LangGraph + FastAPI + Langfuse
description: A LangGraph pipeline that polls 13 companies' ATS boards, throws out the postings that were never going to be relevant before an LLM ever sees one, and scores the rest against an evidence document of what I've actually built — calibrated to tell me no. A real week: 21 postings scored, 2 worth applying to, 19 skipped, with recurring blockers tallied so the rejections double as a study list. Every run is traced in Langfuse, results append to a durable tracker, and the weekly report carries a deterministic health section rather than an LLM grading its own homework.

title: AI Chat Assistant
subtitle: Gemini 2.5 Flash + Cloudflare Workers + Structured Context
description: The assistant in the corner of this page — try it, that's the whole demo. A Cloudflare Worker feeds Gemini a compact, structured reference for the whole portfolio on every request, skipping the vector database the obvious build reaches for. It can also turn a reply into a real UI action — opening the resume, jumping to a section. One eval question caught it confidently repeating a wrong answer: not a hallucination, a bad source file.

title: myPal
subtitle: AAC App Prototype (2021, not actively maintained)
description: An AAC app for kids with autism and speech delays, built for classrooms and homes where the wifi can't be counted on: every card and phrase lives in SQLite on the device first, syncing across iOS and Android only once a connection shows up. The offline-first requirement wasn't a nice-to-have bolted on later — it was the actual constraint the rest of the app had to work around.
